key_insight: Strict causal light cones bound the Fourier bandwidth of shared-parameter energy slices, enabling exact quantum-circuit gradients from fewer circuit settings.
engineering_relevance: For QAOA at fixed depth on bounded-degree graphs, the number of distinct circuit settings for a cost-angle derivative drops from O(m) to O(1), where m is the number of cost terms.
method: Use Heisenberg light cones to bound energy-slice frequencies in layered ansatze generated by commuting local terms.
Recover exact derivatives with a discrete-sine-transform multipoint parameter-shift rule when frequencies lie on a known lattice.
For QAOA cost angles, determine the relevant bandwidth from contact regions in the interaction line graph.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical bandwidth result and circuit-setting scaling reduction, but provides no numerical benchmarks or hardware evaluation.
watch_item: The O(1) setting count assumes fixed depth and bounded graph degree; exact recovery also requires a known frequency lattice and does not eliminate finite-shot estimation noise.
paper_title: Strict Frequency Bandwidths from Causal Light Cones Enable Scalable Exact Gradient Evaluation in Quantum Optimization
